scope: Frozen A0 raw UTF8 unit/stream proof; actual verified A0 seed emitted C and Clang O0/O2 ASan+UBSan/Werror built it. File-backed full-u32 inputs and independent Node Buffer byte/whole-span UTF16 oracles. No public frontend route or arbitrary interior UTF16 mapping claim.

cleanupPolicies.normal: Actual A0 hello/decode/finish; all old allocation capacities/IO unchanged; FINISH drained and zero allocated words. Synthetic status1/5 replies use this usable-runtime policy and are labeled synthetic.
cleanupPolicies.stickyProtocol: A real generic-runtime protocol error is sticky. All old allocations are checked unchanged, then host destroys the unusable session. Allocation-after-FINISH is explicitly not applicable; no successful FINISH claim.
cleanupPolicies.alreadyFinished: Host verifies original allocations then performs actual A0 FINISH before decoder invocation. Decoder returns5 on first LOAD, preserving an already drained/allocation-free session. No post-decode source allocation check is claimed after its storage was freed.

limits: Seven-word relations provide copied-byte identity and whole replacement/UTF16 span endpoints; arbitrary interior UTF16 queries need a separate A0 scan/checkpoint API.
Length0 intentionally performs no LOAD/handle validation; pure unit validates only inspected candidate bytes.
32M-word test budget is not a source cap. Full-u32 physical address-space allocation was not attempted.
Four geometry cases exercise internal append metadata overflow guards, separately from public decoder failure-result clearing.
The component remains private; raw filesystem/frontend diagnostic integration and unpaired host UTF16 transport remain unported.

packaging.note: Import-normalized promotion sources and permanent fresh-seed tests are checked separately; frozen proof is evidence, never a cached-test fallback.
packaging.fixtureNormalization: MJS formatting, declarations and repository-relative loading only; every constructed request, expected output and option row is compared to the frozen 645-case plan. The generic driver remains byte-identical.
